question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=2x$, then 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡5$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $2\operatorname{ln}⁡5$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\frac{1}{6}{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{0}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{e}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{12}{\int }_{0}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{12}({e}^{u}){|}_{0}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡5} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}({e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡5}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\cdot ({5}^{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{24}{12} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
